transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom. My name is Sarah. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Hi Sarah. I'm having a really frustrating issue with my mobile service. My calls keep dropping when I'm at home.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm very sorry to hear you're experiencing dropped calls. I can certainly look into that for you. To start, could I please get your Customer ID number?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Sure, it's CUST-1032.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. And for security purposes, can you please verify the four-digit security PIN on the account?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, it's 8765.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, thank you. I've successfully verified the account for James Gonzalez. Is that you?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, this is James.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great, Mr. Gonzalez. Now, you mentioned your calls are dropping at home. Is this happening everywhere in your house, or in a specific area?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It's worst when I'm downstairs. I have my home office in the basement, and I can barely hold a call for more than a minute before it cuts out. It's impossible to work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can definitely understand how disruptive that would be. Let me pull up our network coverage map for your service address. Just one moment, please.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience. Okay, I see your address here. Our map shows that your area has a strong 4G and 5G signal outdoors. However, what you're describing is very common for basements.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Why is that? I thought you guys had good coverage here.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We do, but cellular signals can be weakened by building materials. Things like concrete, metal, and even certain types of insulation can block the radio waves from reaching your phone. It's what we call signal attenuation.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So my concrete basement is basically a bunker for cell signals. Great. So what can I do about it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, there's actually a fantastic solution. I see you also have our Cymbal Fiber 300 internet service, which is perfect. We can enable a feature called Wi-Fi Calling.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Wi-Fi Calling? I think I've heard of that. How does it work?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It allows your phone to make and receive calls and text messages using your Wi-Fi network instead of the cellular network. Since your Cymbal Wi-Fi signal is strong in your home, it will provide crystal-clear call quality, even in the basement.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: And that's not going to cost me extra, is it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not at all. It's a free feature included with your Cymbal mobile plan. I've just confirmed on my end that it's already provisioned for your line. We just need to turn it on in your phone's settings. Do you have your phone handy?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, I'm holding it right now. It's an iPhone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Could you please open the Settings app for me?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, I'm in Settings.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. Now, please tap on 'Cellular'.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Tapped it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In that menu, you should see an option that says 'Wi-Fi Calling'. Do you see it?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Ah, yes, I see it. It says it's Off.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Go ahead and tap on that, and then toggle the switch for 'Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone' to the on position.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay... it's on. Now a screen has popped up about an emergency address.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, that's an important safety feature. It ensures that if you ever need to dial 911 over Wi-Fi, emergency services will have your correct physical location. Please make sure your address is correct and then continue.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: The address is right. I've accepted. The switch is green now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fantastic. Now for the final confirmation. Look at the very top left of your screen, where the carrier name is. It should now say 'Cymbal Wi-Fi' instead of just 'Cymbal'.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Let me see... wow, it does! 'Cymbal Wi-Fi'. I've never seen that before. So that means it's working?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's the one. It confirms your phone is now prioritizing your Wi-Fi network for calls. This should completely solve the issue with dropped calls in your basement office.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: This is amazing. I wish I had known about this sooner.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm so glad we could get this enabled for you. To be absolutely certain it's working as expected, would you mind if I put you on a brief 20-second hold? I'll have my system call your number back, and you can confirm the call comes through clearly.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Sure, that sounds like a good idea. Go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. I'll be right back. Please don't hang up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, Mr. Gonzalez, I'm back. How did that go?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It worked perfectly! The call came through instantly, and the quality on this call seems better already, actually.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's wonderful to hear! That's the power of using the fiber optic connection for your voice calls. You should have a much more reliable experience from now on.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: This is a huge relief. Thank you so much for walking me through that, Sarah. You've been a great help.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure, Mr. Gonzalez. I'm happy I could resolve this for you today. Is there anything else I can assist you with? Any other questions about your account or services?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, that was the only thing. I'm all set.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Alright then. Well, thank you for being a Cymbal Telecom customer. I hope you have a fantastic rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: You too. Thanks again! Bye.
